<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>An unclassified CIA system was breached in a cyberattack, according to a person familiar with the incident who spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity.</strong>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The breach did not involve any classified information and the issue has been resolved, said the person, who was not authorized to speak by name and spoke on condition of anonymity.



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The breach affected a system that handles open source intelligence, which involves the collection and analysis of publicly available data from sources including the internet, commercial satellites and private data brokers. Though the information is generally public or semi-public, open-source information can give intelligence analysts significant insight on its own or in combination with intelligence obtained from classified spying programs.



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">It was not clear what specific information was compromised or who was responsible.



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The breach was first reported by The New York Times on Tuesday.



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The incident comes to light following a series of highly disruptive system failures that unnerved many Americans. An internal network the National Security Agency uses to communicate classified information <a href="https://www.securityweek.com/classified-communications-network-at-the-national-security-agency-goes-down-defense-official-says/">was offline for a time last week</a>, and the <a href="https://www.securityweek.com/fbi-investigating-apparent-hack-of-its-key-national-criminal-justice-database-ap-source-says/">FBI is investigating an apparent hack</a> of a national law enforcement database that it maintains.<div class="zox-post-ad-wrap"><span class="zox-ad-label">Advertisement. <p class="wp-block-paragraph">Those incidents followed a nationwide ground stop that snarled air travel after air traffic controllers struggled to communicate with pilots. Apple, JP Morgan Chase and Microsoft also had systems go down this month.



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The incidents have put a spotlight on the vulnerabilities inside critical infrastructure, banking systems and the digital tools that millions of people use daily.



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">President Donald Trump’s administration says the series of outages is not part of a coordinated cyberattack and dispatched Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to calm Americans in appearances on Sunday morning news shows.



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Clayton said the outages largely stem from the rush to patch and upgrade systems to stay ahead of hackers who are now empowered with sophisticated artificial intelligence tools to attack at an unprecedented scale.

    CIA system breached in latest cyberattack targeting US intelligence agencies

    Brittney Donovan
    Tue, November 24, 2026 at 9:57 PM UTC
    2 min read
    Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

    The CIA was hacked in the latest cyberattack targeting United States intelligence agencies, according to multiple reports.

    An unclassified CIA system was breached and the attack did not involve any highly sensitive information, a source told The Associated Press. The issue has since been resolved.

    The New York Times reported earlier Tuesday that the CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence recently discovered a cybersecurity breach that exposed some unclassified information. The hacks affected a network that looks for intelligence insights in public, unclassified material.

    It was not immediately clear what unclassified material was accessed or who was behind the attacks.

    Asked about the report, the ODNI said there had been "no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems." The CIA did not immediately comment.

    The breaches are the latest in a series of tech outages and cybersecurity incidents plaguing US agencies, including a breach at the US Department of Agriculture and a temporary outage affecting an internal classified communications network used by the National Security Agency.

    FBI hacked again

    The FBI has been targeted in two separate breaches in recent months, while the Pentagon and the Department of Homeland Security have also been caught up in recent cyber incidents.

    President Donald Trump acknowledged the second breach at the FBI on Saturday, telling Fox News: "We just heard about it, and I will say it's not good. I don't like that. But maybe we'll learn things that we would have never learned otherwise."

    The hack targeted a nationwide database that allows federal, state and local law enforcement agencies to share criminal justice information.

    It came two months after hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen personal information about FBI employees and job applicants from the bureau's recruitment website.

    The breaches at high-profile US agencies follow a string of technology disruptions that affected Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase, the FAA and airlines.

    The failures have highlighted weaknesses in key infrastructure networks, financial institutions and everyday digital services relied upon by millions.

    Trump officials have insisted that the widespread disruptions do not appear to be a coordinated cyber strike.

    Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton tried to reassure Americans Sunday in TV interviews, saying that the breakdowns mostly result from urgent system updates meant to counter cybercriminals who are increasingly leveraging advanced AI tools to launch attacks of unparalleled size and frequency.
